items.title: Art of play in the age of AI
items.content:
Now that code ships faster than ever, you have more time to spend on projects just for the fun of it. Here's what we can learn through that process as developers.

The post Art of play in the age of AI appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.contentSnippet:
Now that code ships faster than ever, you have more time to spend on projects just for the fun of it. Here's what we can learn through that process as developers.
The post Art of play in the age of AI appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.creator: Polly Davidson

summaries.zh: 在AI时代，代码开发速度加快，开发者有更多时间将项目作为乐趣进行探索。这一过程揭示了开发者可通过“玩耍”学习的关键点。文章强调，在AI时代，开发者应重视项目本身的乐趣，从中汲取经验。
summaries.en: In the age of AI, rapid coding enables developers to focus on projects for enjoyment. This "art of play" in development fosters creativity and learning. The GitHub Blog highlights how this shift allows for more experimental and fulfilling work.

items.title: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
items.content:
In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half.

The post Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.  appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.contentSnippet:
In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half.
The post Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.  appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.creator: Ashley Wolf

summaries.zh: GitHub和微软在Codename MDASH试点项目中，将数千份原始AI发现转化为99份经审核的私有报告，并为六个常用开源项目提供了修复建议。维护者已修复其中超过一半的问题。该项目表明，维护者需要的不是更多AI报告，而是具体的修复方案。
summaries.en: GitHub and Microsoft converted thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with fixes for six open-source projects in the Codename MDASH pilot. Maintainers have fixed over half of these issues. The GitHub Blog highlights the need for actionable solutions over raw reports.

items.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
items.content:
Discover how we built the open Agent Host Protocol to keep your agent sessions accessible across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.

The post Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.contentSnippet:
Discover how we built the open Agent Host Protocol to keep your agent sessions accessible across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.
The post Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.creator: Connor Peet

summaries.zh: 本文介绍了GitHub开源的Agent Host协议，该协议旨在实现跨设备会话的持续访问。该协议支持在编辑器、应用程序、手机和云端之间无缝切换，确保用户会话的连续性。该技术通过标准化设备间的数据传输和状态同步，提升了跨平台协作的便捷性。
summaries.en: The Agent Host Protocol is an open standard designed to enable seamless continuation of agent sessions across various devices, including editors, apps, phones, and cloud platforms. The GitHub Blog highlights its development, emphasizing accessibility and interoperability. The protocol aims to unify session management, allowing users to maintain context regardless of the device or platform. This advancement enhances productivity by ensuring continuity in tasks and workflows. The post details the creation of this protocol, focusing on its cross-device compatibility and open-source nature.

items.summary: 本文介绍了GitHub开源的Agent Host协议，该协议旨在实现跨设备会话的持续访问。该协议支持在编辑器、应用程序、手机和云端之间无缝切换，确保用户会话的连续性。该技术通过标准化设备间的数据传输和状态同步，提升了跨平台协作的便捷性。

items.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
items.content:
Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.

The post Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.contentSnippet:
Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.
The post Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.creator: Andrea Griffiths

summaries.zh: 文章《一次性构建，在任何代理上运行：代理技能实用指南》介绍了代理技能的概念。代理技能将可重复的工程工作捕获到文件中，供团队审查和重用，而工具、项目上下文和权限则保持特定于运行它们的宿主。这一方法提高了工程效率并促进了团队协作。
summaries.en: Agent skills enable reusable engineering tasks in files, which teams can review and reuse across different agents. These files maintain tool, project context, and permissions specific to the host agent. The guide emphasizes building once and running on any agent, streamlining workflows while ensuring flexibility. The article is from The GitHub Blog.

items.summary: 文章《一次性构建，在任何代理上运行：代理技能实用指南》介绍了代理技能的概念。代理技能将可重复的工程工作捕获到文件中，供团队审查和重用，而工具、项目上下文和权限则保持特定于运行它们的宿主。这一方法提高了工程效率并促进了团队协作。

items.title: Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering
items.content:
Writing code got faster. The work around it didn't. See how you can plan, write code, review changes, and investigate production issues with GitHub Copilot, and what work still needs your judgment.

The post Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.contentSnippet:
Writing code got faster. The work around it didn't. See how you can plan, write code, review changes, and investigate production issues with GitHub Copilot, and what work still needs your judgment.
The post Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.creator: Nick Liffen

summaries.zh: 文章《超越代码生成：开发者指南：智能工程》介绍了如何使用GitHub Copilot进行计划、编写代码、审查变更和调查生产问题。尽管代码生成速度加快，但相关工作仍需开发者判断。文章探讨了智能工程如何提升开发效率，并指出当前仍需人工干预的部分。
summaries.en: The article "Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering" discusses how tools like GitHub Copilot can accelerate coding tasks but still require developer oversight for planning, reviewing changes, and addressing production issues. It highlights the need for human judgment in the engineering process despite advancements in code generation. The piece appears on The GitHub Blog.
